summary: ObjectGenome validates caster wheelRadiusM only as positive and finite, with no relationship to the referenced moving component or object envelope. An otherwise-valid office-chair fixture can therefore carry an arbitrarily huge finite canonical wheel radius, forcing realization adapters to accept contradictory scale, clamp canonical truth, or invent an adapter-owned validity rule.
evidence: Current src/shared/Objects/ObjectGenome.luau caster validation applies isPositiveFinite(mechanism.wheelRadiusM) and unit-axis checks, but no component/object locality or scale predicate for the radius.

The canonical office-chair fixture uses a 0.028m radius on a 0.09 x 0.08 x 0.04m caster component inside a 0.68 x 1.08 x 0.68m chair envelope, demonstrating the intended manufactured scale relationship.

Current tests/object_genome.luau contains no dedicated wheelRadiusM boundary regression; tests/object_genome_contract_lock.luau focuses schema/ownership/state shape and also has no caster-radius locality case.

PR #480 owns affordance radius locality, PR #466 owns caster swivel/roll-axis degeneracy, and retained decoder work such as PR #395 validates positive caster radius without relating it to construction geometry.
Repository PR/issue searches for wheelRadiusM, wheel radius, and caster wheel radius did not surface a dedicated caster-radius locality repair.

Draft PR #489 records the docs-only finding at exact head 330370641a24984e3de90d22f1195eb916933636; no executable ObjectGenome, Studio, viewport, networking, persistence, or physical-contact evidence is claimed.

metadata.recommendedNext: After the retained ObjectGenome lineage and scheduler explicitly unlock another source depth leaf, define v1 caster radius geometry semantics, add expected-red huge-finite and exact-bound regressions, then enforce one Roblox-independent project-owned locality rule in full genome validation and any standalone canonical caster-record preflight. Prefer a rule derived from moving-component dimensions and/or the object envelope over an arbitrary global magic cap.
